instruction: Generate FiberMesh Hair on a Head Look at `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj`. It contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Head, is a closed UV-sphere-topology ellipsoid (an 'idealized head') roughly 1.8 BU wide, 2.2 BU tall, and 1.8 BU deep, centred at origin. The SubTool has no polygroups, no UVs, no polypaint, and no subdivision levels. Load this OBJ into ZBrush, paint a mask over the top of the head, run FiberMesh Preview to grow hair from the masked area, accept the preview to create a new SubTool named Fibers, and export the result as `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Exactly two SubTools, named Head and Fibers. - The Head SubTool is geometrically unchanged (same vertex and face counts as the input; every vertex position within 1e-4 of the input). - The Fibers SubTool has a face count in the range [15000, 30000] (roughly 3000 fibers with ~6 tris each). - The Fibers SubTool extends upward beyond the head: its bounding-box y-max is at least 0.3 BU above the Head's y-max. - The Fibers SubTool contains at least 2000 distinct connected components (each individual hair strand is a separate component of at least 2 triangles).
